absent: Full net_device layout and its uc, mc, needed_headroom and hard_header_len fields beyond what helpers assume.
Implementations of napi_schedule_prep, __napi_schedule, __napi_schedule_irqoff, napi_complete_done and their scheduling side effects.
Qdisc, neighbour, sk_buff, net, XDP, xfrm, dql, rcu, seqlock and list primitives referenced but not defined here.
Remainder of net_device_ops beyond the shown prefix and semantics of each driver callback.
Numeric values and ordering guarantees for link states, queue states, NAPI states, GRO, rx-handler, path, TC and BPF enumerations beyond relative membership.

findings.text: Legacy device statistics container exposes a fixed set of packet, byte, error, drop, multicast, collision and compressed counters. Each counter is declared through a shared macro giving two views of one storage unit, one plain count view and one atomic count view, so drivers can use either access discipline without changing layout.
Compact core drop accounting holds a small fixed group of drop-related counters only. The whole object carries an explicit alignment request tied to a multiple of pointer-sized units.

Hardware address entry links into both a list and a lookup tree, carries a fixed maximum length address buffer, a use-class tag, sharing and reference counts, a sync marker and deferred reclamation state. A companion list head stores membership count plus list and tree roots, with helpers for count, emptiness, iteration and per-device unicast versus multicast views including sync-filtered iteration.
Address use-class tags are small integer facts distinguishing two fabric scopes and unicast versus multicast roles.

Cached link header object stores a length, a sequence lock and a machine-word buffer sized from a maximum header bound after alignment rounding. Associated facts define the alignment modulus and offset and rounding transforms used to place cached header bytes.

Link headroom reservation derives from device header length plus a concurrently readable headroom value, rounded up to the shared header alignment modulus with one extra modulus unit. Variants cover plain device reservation and reservation with caller-supplied extra bytes.

Link-layer operations table abstracts header creation, parsing, neighbour-based cache fill, cache refresh from device address, header validation and protocol extraction. Creation consumes socket buffer, device, type and address material; parsing and validation are read-only over supplied buffers.

Device link state vocabulary distinguishes start, presence, carrier loss, pending link-watch work, dormant and testing conditions. A small generic receive-merge list object with count is defined alongside.
Receive-merge hash width is a fixed small constant number of buckets.
Per-poll receive-merge node keeps a membership bitmask, a fixed array of merge lists sized by the hash width, a separate linear receive list, a receive count and a cached poll identifier.
Poller configuration stores flush and suspend timeouts, a deferred-interrupt count, a CPU affinity set, a threaded-mode flag and an assigned poll identifier.

Poll instance begins with scheduler state for layout compatibility, then scheduling list linkage, weight, deferred-interrupt accounting, a poll callback, optional netpoll owner, scheduling CPU, device and buffer links, merge node, timer and a tail region that is write-guarded by device management lock plus a control-path-only suffix with thread, timeouts, identifiers, device and hash linkage, interrupt and notifier state and a configuration pointer.

Scheduling list membership is owned exclusively by whoever flips the scheduled marker: the setter adds the instance and the clearer removes it before clearing. Fields after the timer are writable only under device management lock, with the furthest tail restricted to control path use.

Poll lifecycle uses a bit vocabulary for scheduled, missed reschedule, disable pending, netpoll service, list membership, busy-poll eligibility and activity, busy-poll preference, threaded execution and scheduling, notifier presence and threaded busy polling. A parallel mask vocabulary exposes one bit per lifecycle condition.

Receive-merge outcome vocabulary distinguishes merged ownership retained, merged with buffer release, held, normal pass-through and consumed. A typedef aliases the enumeration as the poll merge result type.

Receive-handler outcome vocabulary distinguishes consumed, redirect to another handler, exact match and pass. A typedef aliases it and a handler signature consumes an indirect socket-buffer reference and returns that outcome.
Small query helpers report disable-pending, busy-poll preference and scheduled status by testing the corresponding lifecycle bit.

Scheduling helpers conditionally enter the poll schedule path and report whether scheduling occurred, with an interrupt-disabled variant. Completion is expressed as finishing with zero additional work. Synchronization spins with sleep on multiprocessor builds while the scheduled marker remains set and otherwise orders only through a compiler barrier.

Mark-missed helper succeeds without change when disable is pending, reports not scheduled when the scheduled bit is clear, and otherwise atomically adds the missed marker with compare-and-swap retry semantics.
Transmit queue stop vocabulary distinguishes driver-requested stop, stack-requested stop and frozen states, with combined masks for any stop, any stop or frozen, and driver stop or frozen.

Transmit queue descriptor is split into a mostly read section with device, tracker, active and sleeping schedulers, optional sysfs linkage, rate limit, timeout count and subordinate device plus optional socket pool; a mostly written section with optional queue management state, cache-line separated transmit lock and owner, last transmit time and queue state; and a slow control section with an associated poll instance and optional NUMA node.

Transmit serialization uses a per-queue spin lock isolated on its own cache line with a recorded owner. Scheduler replacement uses RCU-style indirection, and socket pool plus poll pointer are guarded by device operation protection.

Namespace helpers gate fallback tunnel availability and device configuration inheritance on sysctl-controlled values with safe defaults when sysctl support is absent. Queue NUMA accessors expose a stored node only when both queue steering and NUMA support are present and otherwise report no node or ignore stores.

Queue steering maps distinguish CPU-based and receive-queue-based kinds with a maximum kind sentinel. A map object holds used and allocated lengths, reclamation state and a flexible queue index array with sizing and minimum-allocation facts. A device container holds reclamation state, identifier count, traffic-class count and a flexible array of map pointers with sizing facts for CPU and receive-queue dimensions.
Traffic-class queue bound and its selection bitmask are fixed small integer facts.
Per-traffic-class transmit range packs a count and offset pair sharing storage with a single combined integer view.
Fibre-channel host description is a fixed bundle of vendor, serial, version, firmware and model text fields with stated capacities, the model fields being substantially larger than the others.
Maximum physical item identifier length is a fixed small byte bound.

Physical item identifier pairs a bounded byte buffer with an explicit valid length, compared by length plus bounded memory equality. A companion queue-selection fallback signature maps device and buffer plus subordinate device to a queue index.

Device path description tags each hop with a technology kind and device reference plus a variant payload for tunnel endpoints, bridge VLAN handling, switch porting, wireless DMA queueing and encapsulation identity. Stack and context companions bound hop count and VLAN depth, accumulate VLAN tags and Ethernet addresses, and flag wireless handling.

Path technology vocabulary covers Ethernet, VLAN, bridge, PPPoE, switch, wireless DMA, tunnel and wireless LAN hops, with bridge hops further distinguishing keep, tag, untag and hardware-untag VLAN modes. Traffic-control setup vocabulary covers capability query, block and action setup plus a family of queuing discipline and classifier setup operations.

Device BPF command vocabulary covers receive-path program install, hardware program install, offload map allocation and release, and socket pool binding. Execution mode vocabulary distinguishes generic buffer mode, driver mode and hardware mode with a maximum-mode sentinel.

Packet-data-path entity pairs an installed program with its link. A device BPF request carries a command plus a variant payload for program install with flags and diagnostics, offload map pointer, or socket pool with queue identifier.
Wakeup direction flags are single-bit facts for receive and transmit sides.
Transform offload operations table groups device state add, delete, free, eligibility test, sequence advancement and statistics refresh with policy add, delete and free operations.
Interface alias object couples deferred reclamation state with a variable-length alias string. Network-namespace notifier linkage pairs list membership with a notifier block pointer.

Device driver operations table is the dispatch surface for lifecycle, transmit, feature negotiation, queue selection, receive-flag and address-list management, address and MTU changes, control requests, neighbour setup, transmit timeout, statistics retrieval, VLAN membership and virtual-function provisioning. The visible prefix ends inside virtual-function port handling, so later operations are not characterized here.

Synchronization may sleep while polling for the scheduled marker, so it must not run in atomic context. Headroom reservation macros re-read device state and evaluate length arguments at expansion time, so callers must avoid side-effecting arguments and unstable device references.
Depends on an external atomic bit-test helper owned by another dossier.
Depends on an external single-read accessor owned by another dossier.
Depends on an external compare-and-swap helper owned by another dossier.
